verdict.headline: Pangram caught 86.6% of 112 forged paragraphs on the first try, but after forgers revised their work past the detector, evasion jumped to 33.9% overall and as high as 81.8% for one model.
findings: Across all 112 attack attempts, Pangram's first-pass catch rate was 86.6%, but once forger models rewrote rejected text, overall evasion rose to 33.9%.
GLM 5.3 Flash (n=22) evaded Pangram on 81.8% of its attempts after rewrites, including 100.0% evasion on the gov_report document specifically.
Hermes-3 8B (n=30) was caught 100.0% of the time with 0.0% evasion across all three document types, the opposite end of the spectrum from GLM 5.3 Flash.

False alarms on real human writing were uncommon but present: 1 of 30 genuine paragraphs (3.3%) was flagged as AI-written, with that single false alarm occurring on the 1709.02445v2 science paper (1 of 10 genuine samples there).
advice: Treat a 'not AI' result as provisional, not proof: evasion after rewriting reached 81.8% for GLM 5.3 Flash (n=22) even though Pangram's first-pass catch rate was 86.6% overall.
Factor in document type before trusting a score: evasion ranged from 11.8% on the science paper (1709.02445v2) to 50.0% on the gov_report document.
Don't use a single detector flag to accuse someone of cheating: 3.3% of genuine human samples (1 of 30) were false-flagged as AI in this test, so pair any 'AI-written' verdict with other evidence.
